findings.summary: The release helper and the six-member enumeration lived in the emitted scene runtime, far from the struct they enumerate; release_storage and release_geometry_storage now sit beside ModelGeometry in runtime.hpp and the lowerer emits one call.

reclaim_unshared_geometry scanned every mesh record the engine ever created on every removal, and update_mesh_positions ran the same count_if; ModelGeometry::owners, incremented at the one sharing site (the imported-root clone), answers both in O(1).

The owner count decremented per removal while re-add admission was per record, so remove/add/remove of a shared clone could release a sharer's bytes; a removed record is now marked retired before its share is released and re-adding any retired record refuses.

process_working_set_bytes returned a silent 0 on non-Windows, which would let scene -- memory pass a run it never measured; it refuses by name like choose_file, and the psapi pragma went in favour of the kernel32 forwarder.

The two scene loops passed six arguments derived from one cache vector to the memory printer through a single-use helper; the printer is a template over the backend's mesh list and cache, and a records-only overload serves the two sprite loops so platformer and freeciv are measured too.
geometry_mb omitted the morph-target arrays release_geometry_storage frees; they are summed.

spawnNativeCaptured duplicated spawnNativeMeasured's exit contract; one spawn with a captureStderr flag. The optional --backend stanza was spelled three times; optionalBackend serves parity, stability and memory. The fixed delta was hand-typed beside fixedCaptureEnvironment; the memory run spreads it. The demos predicate was the fifth copy; applicationScenes is exported by the registry.

parseMemoryProfile filled a loose record read back with five ?? 0 fallbacks that turned a missing field into a passing zero; samples are typed and a line missing a verdict field is dropped. The settled rule had a dead fallback and a mislabeled frame count; it indexes a third of the way through the samples and the line prints the frame range it judged, with the threshold carried in the summary rather than passed twice.
The 30-frame cadence and the 90-frame minimum were magic numbers coupled across languages; memory_profile_frames / memoryProfileFrames name them and the --frames error says why.
A 12000-entry replay tape exceeded the shell's argument length; --replay-file carries it whole.
The memory run skipped the build-stamp identity check every other measured run applies; it writes and verifies the stamp.

The docs carried the field list twice and stated neither the defaults nor what `all` selects; debugging.md keeps a pointer plus the tool-table row with the defaults, development.md the fields and the two worked commands, and the usage string says `all` is the application demos.
Test regexes pinned whole sentences and statement spellings; they assert the verdict, the numbers and the mechanism separately, and cover --backend, a tape file and a run too short to judge.
owners could fold the retired flag (reclaimed == owners == 0), moving the re-add check from the mesh record to the geometry.
findings.blockedBy: A measurement nobody has taken: a re-added shared clone would need its increment restored and no reached scene re-adds a removed mesh, so the two spellings cannot be told apart by any scene today; the flag stays on the record that is refused.
findings.filedIn: not filed; recorded here as a judgment call

findings.summary: The frame-graph loop (torus-states) prints no memory line, so one of eleven demos is reported as unmeasured.
findings.blockedBy: A measurement nobody has taken: the frame-graph loop has no engine mesh records or geometry cache to report, only a working set, and its own frame counter shape; wiring a working-set-only line there needs a frame-graph scene that streams anything to measure against. The command names it unmeasured rather than passing it.
